Welcome!

I study how China's dominance in clean energy manufacturing, critical mineral processing, and overseas infrastructure finance is reshaping the global energy transition, with a focus on Africa and the wider Global South. My work draws on economics, political science, and environmental studies, and combines causal inference with geospatial analysis of large geocoded datasets.

I am a Postdoctoral Associate in the Science, Technology and International Affairs (STIA) program at Georgetown University's Walsh School of Foreign Service, where I work with Joanna Lewis on US-China competition in clean energy supply chains. I received my Ph.D. from the University of Michigan School for Environment & Sustainability in 2026. My dissertation, *China's Role in Shaping Energy Access in Africa*, examines how Chinese development finance shapes both access to critical minerals and access to electricity across the continent. Before Georgetown, I was a Global China Pre-doctoral Fellow at Boston University Global Development Policy Center. I have also worked in the World Bank in Washington D.C and United Nations Development Programme in Port Louis, Mauritius.

## Research interests

Chinese development finance · Critical minerals · Energy access · US-China clean energy supply chain · Geospatial methods · China in Africa · Energy/Environmental Policy
